q: 1. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinate of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from a common origin, is the most reliable method since errors do not accumulate progressively as they would with consecutive co-ordinates.

q: 2. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all latitudes and departures so their algebraic sums each equal zero (removing closing error) is collectively known as 'balancing the traverse'.

q: 3. A plumb bob is required
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the verticality of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is a versatile tool used for centering instruments, checking verticality of poles, and transferring points down slopes - so all the listed uses are valid.

q: 4. Under ordinary conditions, the precision of a theodolite traverse is affected by
explain: Under normal conditions, angular measurements with a theodolite are quite precise and accidental errors in angle are small; it is the systematic (cumulative) errors in the linear (chain/tape) measurements that mainly govern the overall precision of the traverse.

q: 5. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinates of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse leg
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from the origin, avoids the accumulation of plotting errors that occurs when each point is plotted relative to the previous one (consecutive co-ordinates), making it the most reliable method.

q: 6. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse so that their algebraic sums each become zero (removing the closing error) is called balancing the traverse.

q: 7. In a closed traverse
options: the difference between fore bearing & back bearing should be 90°
the sum of included angles should be (2N-4) right angle, where N is the number of sides
the sum of inclined angles should be (2N-1), where N is the number of sides
explain: The geometric property of a closed polygon dictates that the sum of the interior angles is given by the formula (2N - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 8. In a theodolite the line of collimation is
options: parallel to axes of plate level
explain: For correct instrument geometry, the line of collimation of a theodolite telescope must be exactly perpendicular to the trunnion (horizontal) axis about which the telescope rotates.

q: 9. A 15 cm theodolite means
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm.
explain: The size of a theodolite is designated by the diameter of its lower (graduated horizontal) plate; thus a '15 cm theodolite' has a lower plate 15 cm in diameter.

q: 10. left swing is not much favoured in theodolite survey because
options: most of the surveyors are accustomed to right hand
it is inconvenient to turn the telescope anti-clockwise
vertical scale comes to an inconvenient position to be read.
explain: Since the horizontal circle of a theodolite is graduated to increase in the clockwise direction, swinging the telescope anti-clockwise (left swing) causes the readings to decrease, which is inconvenient for booking and computation.

q: 11. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all the deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) is always equal to 360 degrees.

q: 12. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measured when the traverse goes anti-clockwise.
explain: To measure the internal (interior) angles of a closed traverse correctly and consistently, the traverse should be run in the counter-clockwise direction.

q: 13. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
options: Adjustment of altitude bubble and vertical index frame
explain: The spire test is used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly perpendicular to the vertical axis, by sighting a high point in both faces.

q: 14. The angular error of closure or summation error should not exceed
options: 3√N where N is number of stations or sides.
explain: The standard permissible angular closure error in compass surveying is typically defined as 15' multiplied by the square root of the number of stations.

q: 15. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of interior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: The sum of interior angles of a closed polygon of n sides is given by the standard geometric formula (2n - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 16. According to Bowditch Rule, the correction to latitude (or departure) of any side is equal to
options: Length of the side / Perimeter of traverse
Perimeter of traverse / Length of the side
Total error in latitude / Perimeter of traverse
Total error in latitude x Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse
explain: Bowditch's rule states that the correction to the latitude (or departure) of a side is proportional to the length of that side: Correction = Total error in latitude x (Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse).

q: 17. A traverse deflection angle is
options: the difference between the included angle and 180
the difference between 360 and the included angle
explain: A deflection angle is defined as the angle by which a survey line deviates from the prolongation of the preceding line, calculated as the difference between the included angle and 180 degrees.

q: 18. The process of turning the telescope about the horizontal axis in a vertical plane by a complete revolution is known as
explain: All three terms—reversing, transiting, and plunging—describe the act of flipping the telescope over its horizontal axis.

q: 19. Which among the following is a procedure for computation of traverse area?
options: Calculation and adjustment of latitudes and departures
explain: Computing the area of a closed traverse requires first calculating and adjusting (balancing) the latitudes and departures of all its sides, from which co-ordinates and area are then derived.

q: 20. For adjusting the traverse, which of the following methods can be used?
explain: Bowditch's method (rule) is the standard method used specifically for adjusting/balancing the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse.

q: 21. Which of the following is the accurate method for plotting traverse area?
explain: As with plotting theodolite traverses generally (Q71), the co-ordinate method (plotting each station by its independent co-ordinates) is the most accurate way to plot a traverse area.

q: 22. The projection of a line on a plane parallel to meridian is known as
explain: Latitude is the orthographic projection of a line onto the North-South meridian (L cos θ).

q: 23. In a theodolite the line passing through the intersection of the horizontal and vertical cross hairs and optical centre of the object glass and its continuation is known as
explain: The line of collimation is the specific imaginary line defined by the crosshairs and the optical center of the objective lens.

q: 24. The fundamental lines of transit are
options: horizontal axis and line of collimation
axes of plate levels and bubble line of telescope level
explain: The geometry of a theodolite is based on several axes (Vertical, Horizontal, Collimation, Bubble) being in specific relationships (perpendicular or parallel).

q: 25. If the included angle is greater than 180°, the deflection angle is
explain: An included angle > 180° results in a deflection to the right of the forward-extended line.

q: 26. If the included angle is less than 180°, the deflection angle is
explain: An included angle < 180° results in a deflection to the left (negative) of the forward-extended line.

q: 27. Bowditch rule is applied to
options: an open traverse for graphical adjustment
determine the effect of local attraction
a closed traverse for adjustment of closing error
explain: Bowditch's rule is a standard method for balancing a closed traverse when linear and angular measurements are of equal precision.

q: 28. Direction of closing error in given by
explain: The direction (bearing) θ of the closing error is given by tan θ = (Sum of Departures / Sum of Latitudes).

q: 29. The angular and linear measurement of the part of the traverse can be checked by
explain: Cut-off lines and observations to distant known objects are common ways to verify accuracy within a large traverse.

q: 30. The maximum number of omitted measurements that can be calculated from latitudes and departures of a closed traverse is
explain: Since there are two independent equations (ΣL=0 and ΣD=0), you can solve for a maximum of two unknowns (e.g., one length and one bearing).

q: 31. A deflection angle in a traverse is equal to the
options: difference between the included angle and 180
difference between 360 and the included and 180
sum of the included angel and 180
explain: A deflection angle is computed as the difference between the included angle at a station and 180 degrees, representing the deviation from a straight continuation of the previous line.

q: 32. The line of sight is kept as high above ground surface as possible to minimize the error in the observed angles due to
explain: Keeping the line of sight well above the ground reduces the error caused by both shimmering (heat haze) and horizontal refraction near the ground surface, both of which distort observed angles.

q: 33. For a transit theodolite the least reading on the main scale is 20'. If its vernier scale should read 20, then
options: 59 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal divisions
19 40' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 20' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
explain: To achieve a vernier least count of 20 seconds from a main scale division of 20 minutes, 59 main scale divisions (equivalent to 19 40') are divided into 60 equal parts on the vernier.
